content.value_statement: Product interfaces often become inconsistent when teams lack shared visual rules. This skill supplies a focused dark-mode theme, component guidance, and CSS organization recommendations.
actual_capabilities: Defines a dark primary color palette with background, accent, text, and border guidance.
Specifies Poppins typography weights and readable spacing.
Recommends visual treatment for buttons, cards, inputs, and dropdowns.
Provides animation direction for transitions and named keyframes.
Identifies suggested locations for global, Docusaurus, and component CSS.
limitations: Does not provide implementation code or reusable component files.
Does not define responsive layouts, spacing scales, or accessibility acceptance criteria.
Focuses on a dark primary theme and does not specify a light theme.
Does not validate visual output in a running application.

use_cases.title: Start a product interface
use_cases.description: Use the palette and typography rules when creating a new Physical AI Hub screen.

use_cases.title: Style existing components
use_cases.description: Apply the button, card, input, and dropdown guidance to align an existing interface.

use_cases.title: Review visual consistency
use_cases.description: Compare planned UI work against the documented theme and CSS organization rules.

prompt_templates.title: Apply the base theme
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the UI Design System to describe a dark theme for a new dashboard. Include the background, accent, text, and border colors.

prompt_templates.title: Design a form
prompt_templates.prompt: Apply the UI Design System to a sign-in form. Describe typography, input styling, button styling, and focus treatment.

prompt_templates.title: Review a component
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this card component against the UI Design System. List visual changes needed for color, radius, shadows, and animation.

prompt_templates.title: Plan stylesheet organization
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the UI Design System to propose where global tokens, Docusaurus overrides, and complex component styles should live. Explain each placement.

output_examples.input: Style a primary action button using this design system.
output: Use the teal-green primary accent for the button.
Use rounded corners, a subtle shadow, and a smooth hover transition.
Keep button text off-white for readability.

output_examples.input: Where should styles for a complex dropdown be placed?
output: Keep global variables in the global stylesheet.
Place Docusaurus-specific overrides in the custom stylesheet.
Use a CSS module for the complex dropdown component.

best_practices: Use the documented colors consistently across related interface elements.
Maintain readable text contrast when applying the dark palette.
Keep complex component-specific styles isolated in CSS modules.
anti_patterns: Do not use the accent color for every interface element.
Do not add strong animations that reduce clarity or responsiveness.
Do not place component-specific styles in global files without a clear need.

faq.question: What does this skill provide?
faq.answer: It provides design guidance for a premium dark interface, including colors, typography, components, animations, and CSS organization.

faq.question: Does it include working UI components?
faq.answer: No. It documents visual rules but does not include component source files.

faq.question: Which font does it recommend?
faq.answer: It recommends Poppins with regular, medium, semibold, and bold weights.

faq.question: Is a light theme included?
faq.answer: No. The documented palette is a dark-mode primary theme.

faq.question: Can it guide Docusaurus styling?
faq.answer: Yes. It identifies a Docusaurus custom stylesheet as the location for overrides.

faq.question: Does it test accessibility or responsive behavior?
faq.answer: No. You should validate contrast, keyboard interaction, and responsive layouts separately.
